factual_errors.text: Each kind of atom is a different element, such as carbon or gold.
factual_errors.correction: An element is defined by the number of protons, not by 'kind of atom'. Isotopes of the same element are different kinds of atom, for example carbon-12 and carbon-14, yet they are the same element. The spec says: "All atoms of a particular element have the same number of protons" and "Atoms of the same element can have different numbers of neutrons; these atoms are called isotopes of that element." As written, the sentence contradicts the lesson's own isotope teaching in keyPoints[2].content.

factual_errors.text: An element is a substance made of only one kind of atom.
factual_errors.correction: An element is a substance whose atoms all have the same number of protons (the same atomic number). Its atoms can still differ in their number of neutrons (isotopes). Spec: "All atoms of a particular element have the same number of protons."
